title: Higgsfield Orders ComfyUI to End Open Source AI Challenge Within 48 Hours
summary:
The software company Higgsfield has issued a cease and desist letter to the ComfyUI community, demanding the removal of a project that encourages users to build open source alternatives to its technology. The demand requires the "Open Source Higgsfield challenge" to be taken down within 48 hours, with the company alleging that the use of its corporate name and its chief executive's likeness misleadingly suggests the event is affiliated with the firm.

ComfyUI announced it will not comply with the request and will keep the challenge active, stating that its community is recreating closed applications as open workflows because Higgsfield failed to fulfill a previous promise to open source its own product. The company maintains that it has clearly stated the challenge is not endorsed by or associated with Higgsfield.

selectedTweets.text:
Last night, @higgsfield sent @ComfyUI a cease and desist (attached)

They want the Open Source Higgsfield challenge taken down within 48 hours.

Their argument is that our use of the Higgsfield name and that using their CEO's likeness is an infringement violation (man, the irony). Claiming that it makes the event look like Higgsfield is associated with it.

This couldn't be farther from the truth, which is that Higgsfield made a promise to open source its product and never did.

For the past two weeks, builders have been recreating popular closed apps as open workflows anyone can run.

So we asked our community to deliver where Higgsfield failed: apps in the open, built by the community, for the community. We've made it clear that the challenge is organized by ComfyUI and not affiliated with or endorsed by Higgsfield.

When we started Comfy, we made the community a promise. Our product stays open, free, and yours. We’ve kept it every day since, and one letter isn’t going to change that.

The challenge stays up. Comfy and open source will win!
